2.text: He had the reputation among his neighbors of being dangerous in times of

3.text: trouble; but in ordinary life he was of a quiet nature, and abused nobody.

4.text: “One rich reindeer-breeder was killed by his camp assistant while with the herd. He had

5.text: left three sons, all of them still young boys. The eldest boy, however, was not very small: he had

6.text: already begun to help with the herd during the daytime. There was, besides these, a little brother

7.text: of the one killed. He was of just the same age as the second boy. After the murder, the camp

8.text: assistant, being the strongest man in the camp, slaughtered reindeer as he liked. Then the wife

9.text: of the murdered man began to abuse her eldest son, who slept too long in the morning.¹ The

10.text: woman said, ‘Your father has been murdered, and notwithstanding this you sleep so long in the

12.text: “All this time the boys were shooting with their bows, spurred on by their mother. Their

13.text: little uncle, the young brother of the murdered one, was doing the same. The murderer continued

14.text: slaughtering their reindeer. Very soon he made them poor, and at last their entire herd had been

15.text: butchered. Then the murderer separated from them and went away to a distant locality. The

16.text: boys continued their exercises. At last they grew up to young manhood. The next year they were

17.text: full grown, and became strong men. The murderer went away to the windward side.²

18.text: “Now the boys went in search of him. They had become great archers. They would take

19.text: aim at a blade of grass, and would hit it. Therefore they sought for the murderer. They travelled

20.text: eastward from camp to camp, declaring that they were going to East Cape to trade. The camps

21.text: were numerous in that country, and, after asking among the camps, they at last acquired the neces-

22.text: sary information. The inhabitants said to them, ‘He left his winter place, and is going with a light

23.text: tent to the seashore to get blubber from the Maritime people. His house-mates are travelling

24.text: slowly behind, waiting for his return.’ These young men were without a tent, having only their

25.text: own bodies; i. e., travelling with single sledges, without women and other house-mates. They reached

26.text: the place. Then they began to go every day to watch the trail of the murderer, and every evening

27.text: they came back. They walked on foot, leaving their reindeer in the herd of their host. The whole

28.text: time they carried their bows and quivers upon their backs, ready for action. At last, one day,

29.text: they saw a man coming along the trail with a reindeer-team. Behind him, but at a great distance,

30.text: the usual line of pack-sledges was moving toward them. At last he came nearer and recognized

31.text: them. At the same time he understood their intention, because all of them had bows in their hands.

32.text: Then at last he made a halt. They said, ‘Now we have found you!’ He said, ‘Oh! so it is.

33.text: Oh! better in the camp!’ They answered, ‘Did you commit the deed on our man also in the

34.text: camp?’ So one strung a bow and shot at him. Being an expert archer, he hit him right in the

35.text: middle of his liver.³ It was pierced through. Still he jumped up and ran away, not heeding the

36.text: wound. Another one shot at the running one, and hit him right in the back. Then he fell down.

37.text: They rushed toward him. He was still living, and his eyes looked like those of a living person.

38.text: They hacked him with their large knives upon the head, and broke his skull. The pack-sledges

39.text: were coming. Then they left him, and shouted to those who arrived, “Now we leave to you your

40.text: wild reindeer [killed by us!]’ They started home, running. The wife of the killed man had to

41.text: pitch camp on that spot. Thus they achieved their revenge.

42.text: “After that they left and went home. Then they travelled in this direction, because they

43.text: had lived far inland. When seeking the murderer, they falsely declared in the camps, ‘We are

44.text: going to East Cape;’ and their real intention was to commit murder. Only on the sly did they

45.text: inquire from their own kinsmen concerning the man whom they intended to kill, ‘Where is he?’

46.text: To the other people they said, ‘We are going to East Cape.’ After the deed, they, in their turn,

47.text: left with a feeling of fear.

48.text: “They travelled in great haste. Still summer overtook them, and they had to remain through

49.text: the summer-time. When the next fall came, with the first cool weather they moved right on here.

50.text: They went somewhere on the other side of the Kolyma River, and spent one year there. The
